articleTitle: Research on security screening method based on terahertz imaging and convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The application of teraherz transmission imaging technology plays an important role in safety inspection. The technology is based on the terahertz band, which is able to penetrate common non-metallic substances and reflect metallic substances. The experimental results showed that the average accuracy of each category on the dataset used in this study exceeded 60%, indicating that it showed high accuracy in the identification of dangerous goods. In addition, the average detection speed is less than 25 milliseconds, which indicates that fast dangerous goods detection can be achieved in practical applications. In summary, the dangerous goods identification method based on terahertz transmission imaging technology, convolutional neural network algorithm and object detection has high practicability and feasibility in safety inspection.

articleTitle: LS-UNet: A Lightweight Real-time Segmentation Network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In response to the challenges of low efficiency and extended computation time in road crack detection, we propose a lightweight real-time segmentation model, LS-UNet, built upon improvements to the UNet architecture. This approach utilizes deep separable convolutions to reduce feature redundancy. Furthermore, it incorporates deep skip connections with SE attention mechanisms to extract cross-level encoder and decoder features. Additionally, a hybrid loss function combining the generalized Dice and L1 loss is employed to enhance network training performance. Experimental results on the publicly available DeepCrack and CFD datasets demonstrate that the enhanced method, compared to UNet, achieves improvements in Mean Intersection over Union (MIOU) by 2.99% and 1.84%, with a simultaneous 7% reduction in parameter count and a computational load accounting for only 13%. The frames per second (FPS) reached 33, signifying an enhancement in model detection accuracy and a reduction in both model parameter count and computational load, thereby ensuring real-time requirements are met.

articleTitle: Noise Analysis and Performance of the MEMS accelerometers in Shandong early warning station network
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In Shandong Province, 1230 MEMS accelerometers are deployed, and the site density is among the highest in China. Noise Analysis and Performance of the MEMS accelerometers can effectively guide the selection of site equipment in other early warning system. According to noise Analysis and calculation of earthquake monitoring capacity, the following conclusions are drawn : 1) MEMS accelerometer can meet the needs of earthquake early warning of Shandong early warning station network. 2) The station noise value in 95 % of all MEMS accelerometers is less than -68.5 dB. 3) The accelerometer monitoring capability in 95 % area reaches ML4.0. 4) All MEMS accelerometers effectively recorded seismic signals during the M5.5 earthquake in Shandong Pingyuan County and the first earthquake early warning information output is in 5 seconds after the earthquake.

articleTitle: Modifying Spontaneous Emission Spectra by Using Split Rings
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: We propose a scheme to modify spontaneous emission spectra with split rings. We consider the heterogeneous environment around the dipole and the dipole as a whole to comprehensively explore the impact of the parameters of the system on the partial local density of state. And we achieve the customization of spontaneous emission spectra by engineering the partial local density of state with the co-design of split rings and dipoles for different applications. The finite-difference time-domain numerical results show that our approach is in line with theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional imaging through random media using terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Random media restrict the imaging capability of photoelectric detection devices. Existing imaging techniques through random media mostly operate in the laser wavelength range, while the imaging capability of terahertz waves remains unverified. In this study, we propose a method for imaging through random media using terahertz wave (ITSMUT). By proposing a point spread function of the random media, we performed 3D imaging of volumetric hidden objects obscured by random media. Our method may have potential applications for terahertz devices in non-invasive testing and biological tissues imaging.

articleTitle: Research on Tracking and Localization Algorithm of Motion Target Based on Binocular Stereo Vision
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Machine vision, as an important branch of computer science, has developed rapidly over the past three decades. Binocular stereo vision is an important part of machine vision, and binocular stereo vision can simulate the human eye to provide image 3D position information, but binocular stereo matching is often limited by the environment and can not be accurate 3D reconstruction, and at the same time, the tracker of the moving target in the complex environment has poor robustness. This paper proposes a real-time tracking and localization method for moving objects in 3D space based on a binocular vision information system. Through the optical imaging of the binocular vision system and the improved twin neural network target tracking algorithm, the object-point mapping relationship of the provided mathematical model and the trajectory of the center mass point on the sequence of visual images are obtained. In addition, the outdoor binocular vision-based motion target tracking and localization experimental surface compared with the traditional tracking and localization method, the tracking time of this method is significantly shortened to 90 fps, and the maximum relative error rate between the motion depth value and the actual value of the localization of this method is not more than 0.9, respectively, which verifies the validity and accuracy of the model in this paper.

articleTitle: A Variable Optical Cage Generated by a Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Based on the radiation field of the magneto-electric dipole antenna, we propose a novel method for constructing a variable three-dimensional (3D) optical cage without complex optimization, which further improves the efficiency of optical operations and is easier to implement. Numerical results show that the method generates dark regions with orderly varying sizes, and their shapes can achieve a perfect spherical configuration. Such variable optical cages will facilitate the capture of different particles and atoms.

articleTitle: A High-Symmetry Cobweb-Like Disk Ring Gyroscope Utilizing Rhomboid Spoke
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This paper reports a new type of MEMS disk ring gyroscope (DRG) consisting of 16-sided cobweb-like out-ring, 32-sided cobweb-like inner-rings and rhomboid spokes made by single crystal (100) silicon. Thanks to the linear structure design, the cobweb-like DRG is less sensitive to the fabrication imperfectness. The minimum frequency mismatch can be decrease to as small as 20 ppm(Δf/f) through optimizing the spoke width and rhomboid angle. The proposed gyroscope has 200k Q-factor and is insensitive to fabrication errors, which is promising in industrial applications.

articleTitle: Broadband achromatic polarization insensitive metalens design in the near-infrared spectrum
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Over the past decade, metalens exhibit great potential for applications in compact optical devices. By modulating the phase, amplitude and polarization of the incident light, metalens are applied in a variety of flat optical components, such as micro spectrometers, polarizers and light-field imaging. However, the intrinsic effect of metalens with large chromatic aberration significantly restricts its application in wide-spectrum imaging. Herein, we developed a broadband achromatic polarization insensitive metalens operating in the NIR region in transmission mode. The particle swarm algorithm was utilized to improve the wave aberration by optimizing the reference phase corresponds to each designed wavelength. FDTD simulation was conducted to characterize the focusing performance of the metalens. The focal length of the metalens changes less than 4µm as the incident wavelength is varied from 1µm to 1.4µm. The maximum focusing efficiency of the designed metalens with a numerical aperture of 0.45 is about 43% near wavelength λ = 1.33µm. This research also paves a way for the application of metalens in night vision imaging.

articleTitle: New optical soliton solutions to the Sasa-Satsuma equation with Paul-Painleve approach and extended rational methods
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Purpose: Optical soliton pulses or molecules constitute of the basic fabric for soliton transmission technology, Sasa–Satsuma equation also is given as a model describing this phenomena.Methods: Three approach are applied to catch Sasa–Satsuma equation the solitons to the newly structured, They are the Paul-Painleve approach and the extended rational sine-cosine and rational sinh-cosh methods.Results: Using these methods, we found periodic wave solutions, bright soliton, dark soliton and cusp wave solution. Finally, 3D and 2D graphics of the obtained solutions are illustrated for the applicability and reliability of the prosed strategy for various special values.

articleTitle: Simulation of wall collision relaxation in alkali metal cells for SERF magnetometer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The measurement of wall collision relaxation in alkali metal cells is of significant for a SERF magnetometer. In this paper, the polarization distribution in the alkali vapor cell and the theoretical values of wall collision relaxation are determined through a combined method on the basis of two distinct simulations. The relaxation in the alkali vapor cell is measured by scanning the magnetic resonance linewidth that provides a comparison between the measured and simulated values of wall collision relaxation. The result shows that the relative error between the actual measurement and simulation is within 10% and a reasonable explanation is derived. This research provides a valuable method for the theoretical calculations of wall collision relaxation.

articleTitle: Investigating the Impact of Probe Geometry Characteristics on the Ra in the International Metrology Comparison of Surface Roughness
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: International metrology comparison is instrumental in the establishment of a universal measurement standard and facilitating metrological traceability globally. China, being a major player in industrial manufacturing, plays a crucial role in the global commercial and manufacturing landscape, underscoring the necessity of conducting comprehensive surface roughness international comparison studies. Contact stylus profilometers, widely employed for surface roughness parameter measurement, often exhibit distortions in the measurement outcomes due to the convolution effect created during the probe-surface interface, necessitating consideration of distortions caused by probe geometric characteristics. In this study, we have conducted an in-depth investigation into the mechanism triggered by probe geometric traits inducing changes in the Ra parameter and constructed an algorithm to rectify these measurements, thereby mitigating the influence of probe geometric properties and accurately evaluating the Ra uncertainty triggered by these probe traits. Empirical evidence from this research underscores the efficacy of the devised algorithm in calculating and evaluating the Ra parameter within an international metrology surface roughness metrology comparison context, thereby facilitating effective correction of distorted data.

articleTitle: Efficient thickness calculation for a plate based on space gridding and direction alignment
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Thickness is an important property of plates, and hence should be measured sometimes. It can be calculated from the point clouds measured by some three-dimensional measurement techniques. During the calculation, for any point from one set of point clouds, its matching point should be searched one by one from the other set of point clouds, which is a time-consuming process. To accelerate the thickness calculation, a new strategy characterized by space gridding and direction alignment is presented. It can dramatically reduce the searching scope, and hence improve the thickness calculation efficiency. Experiments showed that the presented method can improve the thickness calculation efficiency by tens of times.

articleTitle: High-accuracy 3D Reconstruction of MEMS Mirrors with Linear Transition Function
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The traditional structured light (SL) 3D imaging method based on a digital light processing (DLP) projectors is often associated with several drawbacks, such as large size, high power consumption. In contrast, Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (MEMS) mirrors present a more advantageous alternative due to their compact size, fast scanning speed, low cost, and low power consumption. In this paper, we propose a 3D SL imaging system based on a uniaxial MEMS mirror, where a linear transition function is put forward to convert the optical model of the MEMS mirrors into a general perspective projection model. Therefore, we can employ the triangulation principle to achieve accurate 3D imaging results directly. Besides, the optimal parameters of the built MEMS mirror SL are obtained by solving a multi-error items energy function. Finally, some relevant experiments were designed to verify the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed mathematical model and calibration method.

articleTitle: Grasping Force Moment Online Measurement of Hydraulic Grab Based on Photogrammetry
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Hydraulic grab is specialized equipment for cargo lifting and excavation, and the grasping force reflects the performance of the grab. Suffering from the complex work condition, it is difficult to monitor the force condition in the oriented-industrial current environment. This paper proposes a novel method to measure the grasping force moment by photogrammetric trajectory tracking, hydraulic pressure sensing and real-time calculation based on force moment equilibrium. This method provides a new way for optimal design, performance evaluation and safety monitoring of the hydraulic grab.

articleTitle: Improved three-frequency three-step phase-shifting method for color fringe projection profilometry
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Traditional three-step three-frequency phase-shifting method needs to project nine patterns, which limits the measurement efficient of the fringe projection profilometry. To address this issue, an improved three-frequency three-step phase-shifting method for color fringe projection profilometry is proposed. The pattern count is two and thus the measurement efficient is increased. The generation strategy of the color patterns is explored. Subsequently, the phase extraction method for the color fringe patterns is investigated. Furthermore, the phase errors caused by color crosstalk are analyzed. The Hilbert transform method is employed to eliminate the errors. Experiments verify the superior performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Excitation Wavelength Selection Method for Fluorescence Spectroscopy of Insulating Oil
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Insulating oil condition monitoring can reflect whether the operation of transformer is faulty to a certain extent, and the dissolved gases analysis technology (DGA) used in the previous insulating oil condition monitoring has serious shortcomings such as long detection cycle, inability to respond quickly in real time, and low sensitivity. Fluorescence has high sensitivity, and fluorescence analysis technology is used to detect transformer faults based on the change mechanism of fluorescent substances in oil. However, most of the existing studies acquire three-dimensional emission spectra, which has the disadvantages of large data volume and long acquisition time compared with two-dimensional emission spectrum data, and lack the analysis of optimal excitation wavelength selection. In view of the above problems, this paper takes Nynas oil Nytro Libra (NL without additives), Nynas oil Nytro Gemini (NG with additives) and Xinjiang Karamay oil, three kinds of insulating oils, as research samples, and carries out two fault simulation tests of interval discharge and surface discharge, and collects the fluorescence spectral data of oil samples under different fault conditions. In view of the problem of multiple fluorescence spectra under different excitation wavelengths of each oil sample, this paper presents a method to select the optimal excitation wavelength based on spectral analysis, analyzes the influence of excitation wavelength on the fluorescence characteristics of insulating oil respectively, carries out the study of optimal fixed excitation wavelength, simplifies the spectral data set, and verifies the optimal excitation wavelength selected by the method with the results of multivariate correction modeling, which has certain reliability. This method solves the problem of huge data set and calculation in the current fluorescence analysis, and maximizes the difference of fluorescence characteristics under various fault conditions, which is convenient for subsequent research to accurately classify and evaluate faults, and provides a theoretical and research basis for the realization of online real-time detection of transformer faults in the future.

articleTitle: Test research on accuracy of laser clearance and video clearance
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: With the widespread application of laser clearance lidar and video clearance monitoring system in wind turbine, the issue of the accuracy in clearance values has become increasingly prominent in wind turbine master-controlled clearance warning system. Based on the different principles of clearance value acquisition by these two types of clearance sensors, a validation scheme for the accuracy of wind turbine clearance values has been optimized and tested in a typical experimental area to assess the differences in clearance values caused by different clearance sensors. The results show that when the clearance values measured by ground-based laser lidar are taken as the actual clearance values, the average deviation of the nacelle laser clearance is -0.16m, while the average deviation of the nacelle video clearance is 1.02m. When the clearance values obtained by ground-based video cameras are taken as the actual clearance values, the average deviation of the nacelle laser clearance is -0.18m, while the average deviation of the nacelle video clearance is 0.85m, Compared with the nacelle video clearance monitoring system, the nacelle laser clearance lidar shows smaller deviations from the actual clearance values of wind turbine, thus demonstrating higher clearance measurement accuracy.

articleTitle: Modelling the human eye and designing presbyopia correction with optical simulation software
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The demands of more advanced presbyopia correction optics are rapidly increasing because of the fast-growing number of presbyopic population. Compared to the more conventional spectacle optics, contact lenses have multiple advantages including a larger field of view and better image quality. Since the contact lenses are not so easily removable, it is preferred to be optimized at multiple viewing distances, which increases its design complexity. In this article, we introduce the full process of designing, optimizing, and evaluating a multifocal simultaneous imaging contact lens for presbyopia correction based on the Chromatic Aspherical Gullstrand Exact (GAGE) human eye model in Zemax OpticStudio. Then, a comprehensive system-level optical analysis is performed on the optimized contact lens together with the human eye model in Speos under a realistic scenario.

articleTitle: Simulation on Focusing of Bilayer Compound Microsphere for Super Resolution Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The microsphere lens holds significant importance in optical nanoimaging, precision measurement, intelligent sensing, and photolithography. The compound structure represents the most essential method for enhancing the super-resolution imaging performance of microsphere lenses. However, the most of prior researches on compound microsphere lenses have been constrained by concentric spheres and bihedra structure theory. In this study, we have introduced the theory of the photonic nanojet (PNJ) and system spectrum extension, which allowed us to simulate the impact of the inner interface profile of a bilayer compound microsphere lens on diffraction focusing. We discovered that a smaller internal interface radius in bilayer compound microspheres is more favorable for optical nanoimaging. These results offer a reliable foundation for achieving higher precision in nano optical detection in the future.

articleTitle: New aplanatic condition and its application for astronomical telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In optical imaging design, sine condition is one of the basic requirements to design an aplanatic imaging system, but sine condition eliminates more sagittal aberration and forms unique comet-like aberration. We imagine an ideal reflector made of sphere, but the focal position can be arbitrarily set on the optical axis, and thus eliminating the meridian and sagittal aberrations to varying degrees. It can be approximately implemented by splicing annular spherical mirrors. We have proved that the best condition to eliminate aberration is to eliminate both meridian and sagittal aberration in compromise, which can reduce the more aberration by almost half than the ordinary sine condition, and be regarded as new aplanatic condition. By using this method, we improved the 2-mirror and 3-plane scheme of the 12-meter astronomical telescope, and the primary mirror is composed of 10 annular spherical mirrors, which can reduce the aberration by up to 55.7% and meet the requirements of astronomical observation. This method can be widely used to improve various existing optical imaging design.

articleTitle: An image processing method to improve DIC reliability based on frequency domain analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Digital Image Correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact measurement method and is also used in turbine blade detection. However, in high-temperature environments, the air inside the turbine engine is heated to produce heat flow disturbance, which affects DIC calculation accuracy. From the perspective of image processing, this study proposes a method based on frequency domain analysis to eliminate the influence of heat flow disturbance on DIC. This method can improve the reliability of DIC and reducing the relative error by about 70%.

articleTitle: Analysis of Thermal Field Distribution Characteristics of Different Structure Submarine Cables in Diverse Laying Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: It is essential to calculate the temperature of conductors according to the temperature of optical fibers in submarine cable for monitoring the temperature of conductors and calculating current-carrying capacity. The finite element model of photoelectric composite submarine cable based on Comsol is established. The thermal field distribution characteristics of oil-filled submarine cable, three-core Cross-linked polyethene (XLPE) submarine cable and single-core XLPE submarine cable in different laying environments including landing section, intertidal zone, seawater and seabed were simulated, the relationship between the temperature values of each part of the submarine cable and the optical fiber in different laying environments was analyzed and studied, so as to obtain the temperature values of each structure inside the submarine cable. The temperature distribution of oil-filled submarine cable, three-core XLPE submarine cable and single-core XLPE submarine cable under typical faults is analyzed. The temperature of the optical fiber is affected by the position, and the temperature of the submarine cable gradually decreases from inside to outside. There is a linear relationship between the temperature of the optical fiber and the conductor core. The expressions of the temperature of the conductor, the outer insulation layer, the outer sheath of the cable and the optical fiber are also established, providing a theoretical basis for temperature monitoring of the submarine cable conductor and calculation of the current carrying capacity.

articleTitle: Fiber coupled system design for quantum secure measurement and control communication
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: A large field of view coupling optical system was designed and optimized using PW algorithm to address the high fidelity space single mode fiber coupling problem in quantum secure communication with large field of view angle reception. A coupling system consisting of four spherical mirrors was designed using Zemax optical design software. After aberration test, the coupling system can realize important roles in the fields of unmanned system quantum communication, optical information processing and fiber optic imaging.

articleTitle: An Edge Detection Model Based on W-Transform Single Pixel Imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: To efficiently reduce the required measurement count for single-pixel imaging edge detection, this study devises an edge detection model based on W-transform single-pixel imaging. In this model, the convolution of the DoG (Difference of Gaussians) operator and W-transform basis patterns as modulation patterns are employed to directly extract edge information from the spectral domain of the target object. Different from traditional methods, it achieves the extraction of edge details from an object without imaging. Numerical simulations and experimental results demonstrate that this model extracts edges with higher signal-to-noise ratios compared to the edge extraction using phase-shifted sinusoidal patterns. Additionally, the proposed model reduces the number of modulation patterns required by half, so as to gain double efficiency. The integration of W-transform single-pixel imaging with edge detection offers a novel approach for edge detections without the need for imaging.

articleTitle: Comparison between contour volume method and DEM grid method in calculating reservoir capacity based on LIDAR data
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This paper focuses on the improved methods and detail solution of producing high-precision DEM and closed contour lines based on LIDAR data. Two methods for calculating reservoir capacity are introduced, one is the traditional contour volume method, the other is the DEM grid method. The calculation results of the two methods are compared and analyzed, proving the importance and high-precision of LIDAR data.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Pollution Monitoring Based on Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Air pollution has serious impacts on human health and the environment, thus accurate monitoring and analysis of air pollutants is of vital importance. As an efficient monitoring technology, the Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer has played a wide role in the study of air pollution. This paper elaborates on the basic principles and working mechanisms of the Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer and discusses the important role in air pollution monitoring, also analyzes the development trend of the Fourier Transform Infrared Spectrometer in air monitoring.

articleTitle: Quantitative Flow Fields Visualization Based on Deflectometry
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: We propose a method for quantitatively visualizing two-dimensional flow fields based on deflectometry. In this method, from the perspective of inverse Hartmann testing, the light rays emitted from the camera travel to the screen after being perturbed by the shock-wave flow field. After obtaining the coordinates of the point source using phase information, we can calculate the deflection angle of the light ray and subsequently determine the distribution of the density field. We provide a detailed description of the principles behind Density Field Measurement Deflectometry (DFMD). In the experiment, we first validated the effectiveness of this method by measuring the refractive index distribution of a GRIN lens. Subsequently, we measured a wedge-shaped model in supersonic wind tunnels, further demonstrating the effectiveness and accuracy of the deflectometry technique in quantitative flow visualization.We compared the experimental results obtained using our proposed method with theoretical results, and the deviation between the two was approximately 2‰. This method offers the advantages of rapid measurement, a straightforward setup, and cost-effectiveness. It introduces a novel approach to measuring the density field of shock-wave flow fields.

articleTitle: Design and polarization characterization of diffraction grating for spectral beam combining
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Semiconductor external cavity spectral beam combining technology is of great significance for obtaining direct semiconductor laser sources with high power, high brightness, and high beam quality, and has received extensive attention from domestic and foreign research organizations. Diffraction grating is a key component in the external cavity spectral beam combining structure. In this paper, a rectangular diffraction grating with a center wavelength of 960 nm is designed, and the effects of the grating period, groove depth, and laser incidence angle on each reflection and diffraction order of the grating are analyzed and the grating is optimized to obtain rectangular diffraction grating with maximum diffraction efficiency of 92.77% for the -1 order. At the same time, the diffraction efficiency of -1 order is more than 90% at the incidence angle of 61° - 63.5°and more than 92% in the wavelength range of 945nm - 972nm, which can be used for high-power laser output to meet the requirements of external cavity spectral beam combining.

articleTitle: Deflectometry for Planar Surfaces with Camera Lens Entrance Pupil Calibration
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Camera calibration is essential in phase measuring deflectometry, and this paper introduces a method focusing on entrance pupil center calibration of the camera lens. The first step involves measuring the entrance pupil length of the camera lens using imaging techniques. Subsequently, the internal entrance pupil position of the camera lens is determined through spatial geometric calculations, utilizing a high-quality reference flat and positioning an external aperture in front of the camera lens. Finally, the entrance pupil center is considered as camera coordinates for measuring the surface under test in phase measuring deflectometry. In the experiment, accurately measurements were conducted on a planar window glass with a diameter of 82mm, achieving sub-wavelength accuracy.

articleTitle: Identification of Residual Layers of Intumescent Fire-Retardant Coating Through Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy and Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: This study explores the utilization of laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) combined with chemometric techniques in fire investigation. We employed two distinct heating devices to generate fire residues from intumescent fire-resistant coatings (IFRC). The residues' top and bottom layers were analyzed using LIBS. We processed the spectral data to minimize variables and applied partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) for categorizing the residual layers. Furthermore, we used principal component analysis (PCA) for visualizing the class separability and identified key wavelengths and their associated elements through the regression coefficients of PLS models. The training and test phase classification accuracies range from 0.944 to 0.992. Notable wavelengths with significant intensity disparities include 251.63 nm (Si I), 251.91 nm (Al I), 387.03 nm (Ca I), and 383.85 nm (Mg I). These findings affirm that integrating LIBS with chemometric methods is an effective strategy for characterizing IFRC in fire investigations.

articleTitle: Areal surface measurement using chromatic focus variation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Optical metrology is an essential measurement technology across various research and inspection domains. Focus variation instruments are widely used in the industry due to their ability to measure steep and high-slope surfaces. The focus variation method extracts an areal surface map by analysing neighbouring pixels' contrast to determine the image focus position in a stack of images. Traditional focus variation instruments mechanically scan the sample surface by attaching the objective lens to a piezoelectric actuator (PZT) for image stack capture. The slow mechanical movement of the PZT poses a limitation for fast inspection in modern advanced manufacturing applications. Additionally, the PZTs' bulky mass and size, and their nonlinear hysteresis motion are other issues associated with the mechanical scanning process. To address these limitations, we present a chromatic focus variation approach that replaces mechanical scanning with a wavelength scanning mechanism. The system employs a chromatic objective lens that determines the image focus by axially shifting the light source wavelength without any mechanical movement. This paper presents the measurement of a 30 µm step height sample using the proposed system. The results show that wavelength scanning is capable of surface measurements, but the current version of the system has a low vertical resolution, which should be enhanced in future versions.

articleTitle: Research on Bonding Method of High Borosilicate Glass Vapor Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In this paper, a five-sided bonding device for a small alkali vapor cell is proposed, using polyetheretherketone (PEEK) material, which is acid and alkali resistant to prevent the corrosion of alloy materials used in traditional tooling. It avoids the problem of brittle and can easily get the slag removal of materials. Its long-term operating temperature reaches as high as 260 °C, which can withstand the annealing process in the chemical bonding process. A detachable upper, middle and lower separable structure is designed, which is convenient for the placement and removal of vapor cell parts, and easy to disassemble and simple in structure. The pulling force and transmittance tests were carried out for the successfully bonded samples, and the average values reached 1 MPa and 85.82%, respectively. This paper provides a practical and effective method for the preparation of small vapor cells for quantum precision measurement based on the interaction of light and magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber from visible to long-wave infrared
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Metallic resonators separated by dielectric films with vertically stacked configurations is a common way to achieve broadband absorption. Here, we theoretically propose an ultra-broadband metamaterial absorber, which consists of an array of nanowire coated with multiple layers of alternating Ti and ZnS nanorings. The average absorption is calculated to be 98.8% in the spectral range of 0.4 to 17 μm. The performance of the proposed absorber is robust against a large change of both the incident and polarization angles. The proposed absorber may find potential applications in photovoltaics, photodetectors and manipulation of mechanical resonances.

articleTitle: An improved Random Sample Consensus algorithm for visual indoor positioning based on angle difference
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) algorithm is a classical parameter estimation and model fitting algorithm, which suffers from poor accuracy and robustness in removing mismatches when dealing with images in complex indoor environments. In this paper, an improvement method of RANSAC is proposed: the mismatch probability of each pair of feature points is quantified by analyzing the angular difference between the SURF feature descriptors, and the mismatch probability is weighted to the stochastic process of RANSAC, in order to improve the accuracy of the matching and the robustness of the algorithm. The experimental results show that the improved RANSAC algorithm is more effective in attenuating the mismatch of images; from the positioning results, the average positioning error obtained by the traditional RANSAC algorithm is 1.09 m, and the average positioning error obtained by using the improved RANSAC algorithm is 0.66 m. Moreover, the probability of the improved method in the positioning experiments with an error of less than 1 m reaches 89%, which effectively improves the positioning accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Spectral monitoring system based on TCS34725 color sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In order to solve the lack of spectral detection means in the lighting industry. A lighting monitoring system integrating optical real-time detection and data monitoring is designed based on the TCS34725 color sensor. The system uses the lamps as the monitoring carrier and the color sensor as the spectrum detection interface. The acquired data is processed by spectral algorithms and monitored through a visualized interface in the host computer. The experimental results show that using the test data of the precision spectral radiometer as a reference, the error of the sensor's excellent coordinates under low brightness environment is less than 5.9 SDCM and the error under high brightness is less than 3 SDCM. The residual of sensor's output spectrum reading is less than 0.15. The mean error of spectral residual value is less than 8%. In general, the system has a small error range, high sensitivity, low cost, simple operation and good stability.

articleTitle: Fast Stereo Matching Based on Gradient-assisted Zero-mean Normalized Cross Correlation
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Zero-mean Normalized Cross Correlation (ZNCC) is commonly applied for stereo matching. However, the ZNCC-based matching could be extremely time-consuming due to its pixel-by-pixel computation. In this paper, a fast stereo matching algorithm based on gradient-assisted ZNCC is proposed. The image gradient is utilized to filter out the ineligible pixels, which reduces the number of the pixels involved in the matching cost calculation. Moreover, the gradient is incorporated into the ZNCC function to enhance the matching robustness. Experiments on Middlebury data sets verify the superior performance of the proposed algorithm, and very effective compromise between the accuracy and computation load is achieved.

articleTitle: A Calibration Method for Biprism-based Virtual Binocular Stereovision with Chromatic Aberration Correction and Structure Parameters Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The chromatic aberration is inevitable in the biprism-based virtual binocular (BBVB) stereovision system. Moreover, calibration accuracy limits the measurement precision of the BBVB system. To address these issues, a calibration method for BBVB with chromatic aberration correction and structure parameters optimization is proposed. First, a chromatic aberration correction algorithm is utilized to enhance the captured images. Then, the intrinsic and the initial structure parameters of BBVB are obtained through coarse stereo calibration. Finally, a nonlinear optimization is employed to estimate the closest structure parameters. The experimental results of length measurement proved the superiority of our method.

articleTitle: High-efficiency polishing of micro-structured NiP alloy using isotropic electrochemical etching for achieving sub-nanometer roughness
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Electroless plated nickel phosphorus (NiP) alloy is an essential engineered material used in optical applications, particularly in the field of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) technology, where high reflectivity of short-wavelength light is required. However, it is still challenging to achieve highly efficient sub-nanometer polishing of NiP plating, especially for micro-structured NiP surface. This study introduces isotropic etching polishing (IEP) as a novel ultra-precision processing technique for NiP plating, which is a damage-free and quick metal polishing technology through the amalgamation of contiguous etching pits. IEP was performed for 4 minutes, leading to the attainment of a sub-nanometer surface exhibiting a Sa roughness of 0.065 nm, which verified efficiency and feasibility of the method. The IEP of NiP plating under various applied voltages is categorized into three stages: the etching state, the limited current plateau state, and the gas evolution stage. Experimental results bear witness to the direct correlation between the material removal rate (MRR) and surface roughness of NiP plating, specifically in relation to the sulfuric acid content within various electrolyte ratios. The most efficacious electrolyte composition was found to be 5:100 (H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>:CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>OH). Furthermore, the technology achieved ultra-smooth and shape-preserving polishing with a surface roughness below 0.1 nm, as confirmed by the comparisons of both the grating microstructure and Fresnel lens before and after IEP. The findings presented in this study are highly valuable for comprehending the process development and viability of IEP for NiP plating.

articleTitle: Infrared-Based Gender Recognition from Facial Images: A Comparative Study Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The gender is an important soft biometric trait of a person, upon which many social and economic functionalities depend or rely. Automatic recognition of the gender of individuals is crucial to many real-world applications, such as public video surveillance, gender-specific access and services, human-computer interaction, demographical studies. Up until now, most research works on gender recognition focus on the visible light, leaving the problem of infrared-based gender recognition scarcely studied. Thus, this research work studies IR facial images-based gender recognition, using deep learning models. We design a CNN model on top of ResNet using a multiscale technique (named as IR-GenderNet). Then, we compare the performance of gender recognition between the visible light and IR bands. We also compare the performance of IR-GenderNet against other methods in the literature that are either traditional or deep learning-based. Experimental results demonstrate that gender recognition using IR is not just feasible but even more beneficial than visible light. It is also proven that the proposed model of IR-GenderNet performs better than all other methods for the problem of IR-based gender recognition. Lastly, cross-dataset experiments also justify the generalization ability of IR-based gender recognition using the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Vision System for High-Speed Railway Turnout Monitoring with a Robust Laser Stripe Centerline Extraction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: On-line automatic monitoring of turnout status of the high-speed railway (HSR) is a key element toward the development of a modern railway safety system that provides enhanced security and efficiency. Typically, the monitoring approaches of railway turnouts either indirectly measured by data fusion of multiple sensors or directly measured by hand-held instruments. The former approach suffers from low accuracy and reliability, whereas the latter method with drawbacks of being unable to work online, all-weather, and inefficient. In contrast, this paper presents an on-line turnout monitoring approach based on active stereo-vision system. After briefly introducing the measuring principle, a laser stripe image processing pipeline is investigated. Our main contribution is proposing a robust algorithm for extracting the center of laser stripes based on Kalman Filtering and Topological Geometry (KFTG) strategy according to the special intensity profile of industrial laser, which achieves stable results in the vibration state of laser stripes. Besides, the laser image noise is smoothed by the S-Box filter, which uses Side-windows scanning policy to preserve the geometric information of the fringe edge, thereby, benefits to the status parameters output. Finally, the experimental results demonstrate that the KFTG algorithm is robust against the challenges of strong noise and vibration, and proposed vision system has a measurement accuracy of 0.45 mm in harsh environments.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Fiber Optic Continuum Robot (MFOCR) for 3D Map Reconstruction, Obstacle Avoidance and Path Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: Fiber optic sensors based on intensity modulation technique measure the intensity of reflected light using a pair of adjacent optical fibers and a reflector to infer changes in displacement. The simplicity of the sensing device design makes it easier to apply in small-scale surgery, integrating with invasive surgery, endoscopic approach, etc. And the magnetic continuum robot, as a major focus of current research in small-scale surgery, can be deeply integrated with fiber optic sensors to provide it with stronger sensing capabilities to achieve complex functions. Herein, we introduce a magnetic fiber optic continuum robot (MFOCR) integrated with a reflective fiber optic sensor, which can be controlled to deflect using a three-axis Helmholtz coil platform and translated using a three-axis slide. Experimental results show that the ranging capability of the MFOCR enables 3D map reconstruction, obstacle avoidance, and path selection functions. Moreover, the system exhibits potential for autonomous navigation and environmental awareness in unknown environments.

articleTitle: Study on measurement method of high-speed dynamic pose based on inertial measurement unit and laser tracker
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: To improve the measurement accuracy of laser target measurement system for high-speed movement, this paper introduces a high precision laser tracker and inertial measurement unit (IMU) to construct a combined measurement system. The laser tracker is utilized as the base station, and the accurate positioning of laser target can be achieved by combining the appropriate pinhole prism. The IMU is installed inside the laser target. When the laser target is constantly moving, the system introduces the measurement value of IMU to the quaternion differential equation for the real-time attitude estimation. By establishing the SINS state equation and the Kalman fusion filter equation, the laser target can be used to correct the error accumulation of IMU to prevent the precision divergence. Experiments results indicate that the combined measurement system of positional deviation is better than ±0.1 mm and attitude deviation is better than 0.02°, which demonstrates that the combined system based on IMU and laser tracker is more flexible and reliable and can meet the requirements of high-speed target measurement under the dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Denoising Algorithm of Single Photon Laser Altimetry Data for On Orbit Processing
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: The new generation of laser mapping satellite represented by ICESat-2 adopted multi-beam photon counting detection technology. A large amount of noise was attached to the detection data, which brings challenges to the satellite-ground transmission and subsequent processing. For the application requirement of efficient on orbit processing, a multi-level joint denoising method based on local photon elevation histogram statistical filtering was proposed. First, the obvious noise photons were eliminated by rough surface elevation threshold. Second, elevation histogram statistical filtering and threshold adaptive correction method were used to achieve precise denoising. Comprehensively the method was verified on MABEL laser altimetry data. The verification results indicate that the proposed method has efficient denoising ability and dynamic adaptability, data processing can be carried out under all-day condition of different point cloud density and the average noise elimination rate is above 86% for the daytime’s strong noise under the condition of near lossless retention of effective photons, which realizes efficient denoising of raw data. The use constraints of previous classical algorithms on observation time, photon density, terrain slope, etc have been synchronously improved. Therefor it can be a reference for the design of on-orbit processing algorithm of spaceborne single photon laser altimetry radar.

articleTitle: Effect of adhesive on surface accuracy and adaptability analysis of large aperture rectangular mirror
publicationTitle: 2023 2nd International Conference on Optical Imaging and Measurement (ICOIM)
abstract: In order to quickly obtain the effect of different bonding processes on mirror surface shape, the process of adhesive curing and shrinking was simulated. Firstly, according to the free curing model of colloid, the functional relationship between mirror deformation and adhesive shrinkage was derived. Then, based on the temperature loading method, the finite element model of adhesive curing shrinkage was established, and the influence of adhesive quantity, adhesive position, distribution mode and colloidal parameters on the surface shape of large aperture rectangular mirror was analyzed, and the optimization scheme of high surface shape precision bonding was obtained. In the process of rectangular mirror assembly design, the influence of whether there is a frame on the mirror surface shape simulation results was compared. The mirror surface shape was taken as the response constraint, and topology optimization of the frame was carried out to obtain a lightweight configuration for post-processing, including smooth and smooth processing, structural reconstruction processing and optimal configuration of frame materials. The weight of the frame was 7.93 kg. Compared with direct structural reconstruction, the optimized configuration of frame materials reduced the weight by 62.12%. The results show that the PV value of the mirror surface is 53.26 nm, the RMS value is 10.98 nm, and the maximum stress value is 0.04 Mpa when the side 6-point flexible bond ring is used, the non-uniform near-homogeneous surface distribution, the colloid diameter is 10 mm, and the colloid thickness is 0.1 mm. Finally, the environmental adaptability of the mirror assembly is analyzed, which satisfies the Rayleigh criterion of the optical system and the mechanical conditions of the structural design. The research results can provide reference for the optimization scheme of high surface shape precision bonding of large aperture rectangular mirror and the optimal design of support structure.
